name: Onesimus shares prevention knowledge
description: Onesimus, an enslaved African in Massachusetts, shared knowledge of an existing smallpox prevention practice with Cotton Mather in 1716.

date.basis: Date refers to the scoped documented case, not global origin.

events.statement: Onesimus, an enslaved African in Massachusetts, shared knowledge of an existing smallpox prevention practice with Cotton Mather in 1716.

evidence.supports: WHO reports that Onesimus, an enslaved African, told Cotton Mather about an existing prevention practice in 1716; Mather later advocated it during the 1721 Massachusetts outbreak. This dates a knowledge transfer and says neither who invented it nor when Onesimus learned it.

events.caveats: The date is the documented knowledge transfer, not the origin of the practice or a documented treatment event. The practice carried risks and was distinct from later vaccination.
